title: Drishyam 3 Opens Tomorrow With ₹29 Crore in Pre-Sales — But Nobody Knows Where NRIs Will Stream It
excerpt: A Delhi High Court order, an Amazon-vs-producer standoff over OTT rights, a South Korean remake deal, and an Ajay Devgn Hindi version in October — the Drishyam franchise is expanding everywhere except the one place diaspora audiences want it most: a confirmed streaming date
body:
Mohanlal’s *Drishyam 3* hits theatres worldwide on May 21, 2026, carrying ₹29 crore in advance bookings and the weight of being one of Malayalam cinema’s most anticipated finales. The numbers are staggering — it is already the second-highest pre-sale in Mollywood history, trailing only *L2: Empuraan* at ₹52.5 crore. But behind the box office euphoria lies an unresolved legal battle that has left one critical question unanswered: when and where will diaspora audiences who can’t make it to a cinema actually watch this film?

## The Amazon Standoff

In April, the Delhi High Court granted interim relief to Amazon Prime Video after the streaming giant filed a plea against Aashirvad Cinemas, Mohanlal’s production banner. Amazon claims it holds exclusive or first-preference streaming rights to the Drishyam franchise under an earlier agreement — the same deal that made *Drishyam 2* a direct-to-OTT release on Prime Video in 2021 during the pandemic.

The court’s order temporarily restrains the producers from negotiating or finalising any OTT deal with third parties. In practice, this means the film’s digital premiere — typically announced within days of a theatrical release for a title of this magnitude — is in legal limbo.

For NRIs who watched *Drishyam 2* on Prime Video from their living rooms in Edison, Brampton, and Southall, this is more than an industry dispute. It’s the difference between watching the franchise’s conclusion in weeks versus months.

## The Box Office Is Not the Problem

The theatrical release itself is proceeding without any legal complications. *Drishyam 3*, directed by Jeethu Joseph with a returning cast including Meena, is releasing simultaneously in Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, and Kannada dubbed versions. The ₹29 crore advance booking figure reflects demand across all four languages and overseas markets.

In North America, the film has crossed $160K in pre-sales with a projected $265K opening day. For a Malayalam-language film — even one as iconic as Drishyam — these are extraordinary numbers that reflect the franchise’s crossover appeal.

The release also carries personal significance: May 21 is Mohanlal’s birthday, and the convergence of the release date with the actor’s 66th birthday has amplified marketing and fan enthusiasm. Co-stars Manju Warrier and Prithviraj Sukumaran publicly wished him ahead of the premiere, framing it as both a professional milestone and a celebration.

## Going Global — Without Streaming Clarity

While the OTT situation remains unresolved, the Drishyam franchise is expanding in other directions. A South Korean remake has been confirmed, marking one of the few Indian film properties to be adapted for the Korean market — a reversal of the usual flow where Korean dramas and thrillers get Indian remakes.

Meanwhile, the Hindi remake of *Drishyam 3* starring Ajay Devgn is officially slated for October 2, 2026. The Hindi *Drishyam 2* (2022) earned over ₹240 crore at the Indian box office, making the franchise one of the most commercially reliable adaptation pipelines in Indian cinema.

## What This Means for NRI Audiences

The practical impact is straightforward. If you’re in a city with a Malayalam-language or dubbed screening — and most major NRI metros will have them — you can watch *Drishyam 3* in theatres from May 21. The film is releasing in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, and the Gulf on the same date.

But if you’re waiting for the OTT release — and many diaspora viewers, especially older family members and those in smaller cities, do exactly that — there is no confirmed date, no confirmed platform, and an active court case preventing one from being announced.

The Delhi HC matter is expected to be heard again in coming weeks. Until then, Georgekutty’s final chapter has a premiere date but no streaming home — an uncomfortable position for a franchise that quite literally pioneered the pandemic-era direct-to-OTT model in Indian cinema.
